category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title = 'When the child names ONE part of a multi-part structure — repairing the partial-decompose trap at Grade 3'. The trap is real and grade-appropriate, and recovery_moves ['Trace each part.', 'Drill bottom to top.', 'Compare full vs partial.'] are concrete. But there is no named research citation, and recovery does not branch by what the diagnostic told you about the child.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite a named source for the partial-decompose trap (Battista 2007 on spatial structuring, or Sarama & Clements 2009 on composition/decomposition trajectories) in the rationale. Then split recovery_moves into two diagnostic branches: (a) if child names parts when you trace one-by-one but not on their own → drill 'bottom-to-top scan' as a self-cuing routine; (b) if child cannot see hidden/back parts at all → use a physical solid the child can rotate before returning to the 2D structure card.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Solid Cards (1 set per pair)' and 'Structure Cards (12)' as required, and differentiation.for_movement_learners says 'Build with real classroom objects' but this is not framed as a complete no-paper alternative path. The lesson does not offer an explicit NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE version a teacher could run on a day when prep wasn't possible.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a 'No-materials version' bullet under differentiation: children compose structures using their own bodies and classroom items (book = rectangular prism, marker = cylinder, paper cup = cone, balled-up paper = sphere); decompose by walking around a real classroom object (chair, desk, recycling bin) and naming each 3D part out loud. Make explicit that the activity runs with zero printed cards.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: minds_on teacher_script presents one teacher-modelled decomposition ('A house: rectangular prism (body) + square pyramid (roof)') and pairs follow the same template. There is no moment where children INVENT or COMPARE alternative decompositions of the same structure, and the expanded_walkthrough does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms (no reference to Battista's spatial structuring or Sarama & Clements composition levels).
category_feedback.required_fix: In the action phase, add a 'Two ways to build it' step: pairs compose the SAME target structure two different ways (e.g., a 4-block tower as cube+cube+cube+cube vs cube+rectangular-prism+cube), then compare which decomposition is 'easier to see' and why. In expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the trap as a level shift on Sarama & Clements' composition trajectory (pre-composer → piece-assembler → picture-maker → shape-composer) so a substitute teacher knows what level the child is operating at.

summary_note: Strong pair on alignment, voice, and lesson-worksheet match. Three categories sit at Achieving (3) but not Exceeding (4): the partial-decompose trap needs a research citation and a branching recovery; the lesson needs an explicit no-paper alternative; and the math needs a strategy-comparison move plus research-named misconception language. All three fixes land in lesson_02; worksheet is fine as-is.
